nodes.content: Develop streaming speaker diarization that preserves speaker identities through overlap and long absences without revising committed labels.
requirements: Achieve 15% lower overlap-inclusive diarization error than an equally latency-constrained baseline on held-out conversational audio.
Commit labels within 500 milliseconds while handling unseen speakers without a known speaker count.

nodes.content: Use causal multi-label embeddings, persistent speaker prototypes, and novelty-gated slots; commit overlap-aware assignments every 400 ms without revision.
Can novelty-gated persistent prototypes distinguish returning speakers after 20-minute absences from unseen speakers during overlap within 400 ms?
On held-out 20-minute-gap overlap segments, novelty-gated prototypes achieve ≥85% returning-speaker recall and ≤10% unseen-speaker false matches within 400 ms.
Build held-out GapOverlap-20 with 20-minute absences and unseen arrivals during overlap; measure return recall and false matches at 400 ms.
On GapOverlap-20, 400-ms assignments reached 87% returning-speaker recall and 8% unseen-speaker false matches during overlap after 20-minute absences.
Retain novelty-gated persistent prototypes for streaming trials; GapOverlap-20 meets both identity thresholds at 400 ms.
Integrate retained prototypes with causal overlap decoding; compare held-out overlap-inclusive DER against a 400-ms baseline, auditing irreversible unseen-speaker assignments.
Benchmark the prototype decoder and 400-ms baseline on held-out CallMix-Overlap; log overlap-inclusive DER, commit latency, revisions, and unseen-speaker assignments.
CallMix-Overlap report records prototype versus baseline overlap-inclusive DER of 20.0% versus 24.0%, 400-ms commits, zero revisions, and unseen-speaker assignment logs.
On GapOverlap-20, simultaneous-onset overlap reduced returning-speaker recall to 79% versus 87% overall at 400 ms.
Novelty-gated prototypes retain ≥85% returning-speaker recall during simultaneous-onset overlap after 20-minute absences with 400-ms assignments.
Derive coarrival error strata from CallMix-Overlap report logs; measure 400-ms returning-speaker recall across GapOverlap-20 simultaneous-onset strata.
CallMix-Overlap-guided GapOverlap-20 analysis found 74% returning-speaker recall for onset gaps under 100 ms at 400-ms commits, below 85%.
Train a causal two-source separator for sub-100-ms coarrivals; gate prototype updates and retest 400-ms recall and overlap-inclusive DER.
Train a causal two-source separator on sub-100-ms coarrivals; test gated-prototype recall on GapOverlap-20 and DER on CallMix-Overlap at 400 ms.
Gated Separator-v2 checkpoint and report record 86% sub-100-ms return recall and 19.2% CallMix-Overlap overlap-inclusive DER at 400 ms.
Audit Separator-v2 on GapOverlap-20 sub-100-ms coarrivals after 20-minute absences; measure return recall and unseen-speaker false matches at 400 ms.
Use a causal Bayesian speaker-state filter with dormant identity priors, open-set birth moves, and multi-speaker likelihoods for irreversible 450-ms labeling.
How should the filter calibrate dormant-speaker versus new-speaker posterior odds during overlap without inflating false births at 450 ms?
Duration-conditioned dormant-to-birth odds yield ≥85% returning-speaker recall and ≤5% false births on GapOverlap-20 overlaps at 450 ms.
Fit duration-conditioned odds from CallMix-Overlap report logs; measure 450-ms returning-speaker recall and false births on GapOverlap-20 overlaps.
On GapOverlap-20 overlaps, duration-conditioned odds achieved 88% returning-speaker recall and 4% false births with 450-ms commits.
Using GapOverlap-20-validated odds and CallMix-Overlap baseline logs, test 450-ms return recall and false births across withheld overlap sessions.
On withheld GapOverlap-20 overlap sessions, 450-ms commits yielded 81% returning-speaker recall and 7% false births, missing both thresholds.
Adding separation-confidence calibration to dormant-birth odds yields ≥85% return recall and ≤5% false births on withheld GapOverlap-20 at 450 ms.
Combine CallMix-Overlap baseline logs, original GapOverlap-20 odds, and withheld-session errors; test confidence-calibrated recall and false births on fresh 450-ms overlaps.
On fresh GapOverlap-20 overlap sessions, confidence-calibrated odds achieved 86% returning-speaker recall and 4.5% false births at 450 ms.
Advance calibrated odds to DER trials: duration-only odds passed initial validation but failed withheld sessions; calibration passed fresh sessions.
Compare calibrated filter with a 450-ms baseline on held-out CallMix-Overlap; require ≥15% lower overlap-inclusive DER, zero revisions, unrestricted speaker births.
Run calibrated filter and equal-latency baseline on held-out CallMix-Overlap; log overlap-inclusive DER, birth counts, 450-ms commits, and label revisions.
CallMix-Overlap benchmark report records 19.6% versus 23.5% overlap-inclusive DER, 450-ms commits, zero revisions, and unrestricted speaker births.
Train a recurrent speaker-slot transformer with gap-replay contrastive loss and open-set slot spawning, committing multi-label frames after 480 ms.
Can gap-replay contrastive training prevent dormant slot swaps when returning and unseen speakers overlap at 480-ms commits?
Gap-replay training reduces dormant slot swaps by ≥30% versus standard slot training on GapOverlap-20 return-and-unseen overlaps at 480 ms.
Reuse the filter’s CallMix-Overlap scoring protocol; compare gap-replay against standard slots for GapOverlap-20 swaps at 480 ms.
On GapOverlap-20 return-and-unseen overlaps, gap-replay cut dormant slot-swap rate from 12.0% to 7.8% at 480 ms.
Replicate the GapOverlap-20 slot-swap comparison on withheld sessions at 480 ms, using gap-replay training and the CallMix-Overlap scoring protocol.
On withheld GapOverlap-20 sessions, gap-replay reduced slot swaps from 11.5% to 9.2% at 480 ms, only 20% lower.
Coarrival-focused hard-negative gap replay reduces dormant slot swaps by ≥30% versus standard training on withheld GapOverlap-20 at 480 ms.
Use CallMix-Overlap scoring and swap analyses to train coarrival negatives; compare fresh GapOverlap-20 swaps against standard slots at 480 ms.
On fresh GapOverlap-20 sessions, hard-negative replay reduced dormant slot swaps from 11.0% to 7.1% at 480 ms, a 35% reduction.
Advance hard-negative replay to DER testing: ordinary replay’s initial 35% gain fell to 20% withheld; hard negatives achieved 35% fresh.
Benchmark hard-negative slots against an equal-latency baseline on held-out CallMix-Overlap; require ≥15% lower overlap-inclusive DER and revision-free 480-ms commits.
Reuse the CallMix-Overlap report’s scoring protocol; run hard-negative slots and a 480-ms baseline, recording overlap-inclusive DER, revisions, and speaker births.
CallMix-Overlap report records 19.4% versus 23.3% overlap-inclusive DER, 480-ms commits, zero revisions, and open-set speaker births.
Using initial, withheld, and hard-negative swap findings, stratify CallMix-Overlap report errors by return–unseen overlap; recompute DER and slot-swap rates.
On CallMix-Overlap return–unseen overlaps, hard-negative slots yielded 25.1% versus 31.8% overlap-inclusive DER and 7.3% versus 11.4% slot swaps.
Keep hard-negative slots as the deployment candidate: return–unseen overlap DER fell 21%, corroborating the earlier swap-based decision.
